title: Naver, Brookfield and Nvidia launch $9B AI factory plan in South Korea
summary: Naver, Brookfield, and Nvidia partner to launch a 9 billion dollar AI factory in South Korea
detailed: Naver is teaming up with Brookfield to secure artificial intelligence (AI) computing infrastructure.
The partnership is part of a 1GW-class global AI factory project pursued by Naver, NVIDIA, and Brookfield.

Under the agreement, Brookfield will establish a special purpose vehicle (SPV) tentatively called "Asset Co." The entity will invest up to $9 billion to secure infrastructure such as graphics processing units (GPUs) and data centers and will supply computing resources to Naver Cloud, the operator.

sentences: Naver is teaming up with Brookfield to secure artificial intelligence (AI) computing infrastructure.
Brookfield will invest in facilities, and Naver Cloud will use them to operate the business.

Naver said on the 27th that with this contract it has met the precondition for receiving NVIDIA's strategic equity investment and plans to quickly wrap up the related paid-in capital increase procedures.
The partnership is part of a 1GW-class global AI factory project pursued by Naver, NVIDIA, and Brookfield.
An AI factory is infrastructure that uses large-scale computing resources to carry out AI model training and inference.
The three companies plan to combine capital and operating capabilities, as well as technology, to speed up execution.

Under the agreement, Brookfield will establish a special purpose vehicle (SPV) tentatively called "Asset Co." The entity will invest up to $9 billion to secure infrastructure such as graphics processing units (GPUs) and data centers and will supply computing resources to Naver Cloud, the operator.
Naver and Naver Cloud will lead the project based on their experience building and operating GPU clusters and managing data centers.
They plan to start operations in the first half of 2027 at 55MW and expand to 200MW in 2028.
Using the hyperscale data center "Gak Sejong" as a key base, they will gradually enter overseas markets.
Gak Sejong is Naver's second in-house data center, which began operations in Nov.
It was built on a site of about 294,000 square meters to accommodate up to 600,000 server units.

Its server capacity is about six times that of the first in-house data center, "Gak Chuncheon." Naver built Gak Sejong by combining the experience accumulated over 10 years of operating Gak Chuncheon with AI, cloud, robotics, and Autonomous Driving technologies.
NVIDIA will lead technology collaboration on next-generation high-performance computing platforms, including DSX.
The aim is to improve the AI factory's performance and infrastructure operating efficiency.
Naver will conduct a third-party allotment paid-in capital increase for NVIDIA, with specific terms to be disclosed later.
Naver expects this structure to help reduce the initial financial burden.
The company said it designed the plan to lower the upfront investment needed to directly secure large-scale facilities and to pay infrastructure usage fees tied to business revenue.
Based on this, its strategy is to secure both operational stability and business scalability.
However, Naver decided to provide a payment guarantee for up to eight years for its subsidiary Naver Cloud's obligation to pay usage fees.
The company said the step is intended to support smooth execution of the contract and that providing the guarantee does not immediately mean actual cash expenditure or expense.
Naver plans to respond to AI computing demand at home and abroad and expand its business base in the global infrastructure market, based on the three companies' long-term cooperation.
